title: Turtle long cost / slippage sensitivity
verdict_detail: Cost robustness is NOT met by the volatility-scaled arm (stress PF 1.037 < 1.05); met by the fixed-notional arm (1.259). Mixed by sizing -> not a clean pass.
correction_note: First run silently excluded funding (SI-4). Re-run after downloading 1h mark; the volatility-scaled arm's stress PF dropped from 1.051 to 1.037, below the 1.05 acceptance threshold, changing the verdict from PASS to FAIL.
scope_note: Cost result only. Does not overturn P3-EXP-001's out-of-sample FAIL.

preregistered_grid.effective_cost_equals: fee + slippage (freqtrade models slippage via the fee)

key_findings: Full-sample PF degrades monotonically with cost for both arms.
Cost robustness holds for fixed-notional sizing (stress PF 1.259) but NOT for volatility-scaled sizing (1.037).
Sizing dominates cost exposure: long_raw pays 10.4k USDT fees at stress with PF 1.259 / DD 28.7%; long_vol pays 114.7k with PF 1.037 / DD 83.7%.
The out-of-sample window is negative at every cost level (PF 0.63-0.66 at stress).
decision: FAIL. The preregistered cost-robustness criterion (full-sample PF >= 1.05 at stress) is met by fixed-notional sizing but NOT by volatility-scaled sizing, so the experiment does not robustly pass. Costs are not the cause of failure; the failure is out-of-sample (P3-EXP-001). No promotion or combination is authorised.
